Definition: middle voice from G1909 and the base of G4649; to inspect, i.e. (by implication) to select; by extension, to go to see, relieve:--look out, visit.
BiblicalUsage: Episkeptomai means to visit, to look upon, to inspect with care. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for He hath visited and redeemed His people; God hath visited His people, the crowd says at Nain; I was sick, and ye visited me; let us go again and visit our brethren; and pure religion is to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction.
TheologicalSignificance: He visited us in Christ, and pure religion is visiting those He loves — the sick, the fatherless, the widow — in theirs. I believe visiting is God's own pattern, and the visit is where the gospel stops being words.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; James, Brother of Jesus; Paul; Barnabas
RelatedEvents: The Raising of the Widow's Son at Nain
